gomod.description: Run `go mod tidy` after every Go update. Without it Renovate records only the /go.mod hashes for a bumped version, so go.sum ends up missing the module-zip (h1:) hashes and keeps superseded entries. Tool-only modules break outright, because `go install` runs in -mod=readonly.

packageRules.description: Renovate skips `// indirect` Go modules unless told otherwise, so a security fix in a transitive module (grpc GO-2026-6443, reached through terraform-plugin-go) never produced a PR and only surfaced as a govulncheck failure on main. Enabling them also lets Renovate's vulnerability-alert PRs, which bypass minimumReleaseAge and grouping, act on them. Kept free of matchUpdateTypes on purpose: rules are applied once before lookup, when the update type is unknown, so a rule that combines the two never matches and the modules stay disabled.

The importing module picks the major module path, so rewriting an indirect requirement to /v2 only produces an unused line that `go mod tidy` removes. Evaluated after lookup, once the update type is known.

The Go vulnerability database's range for GO-2026-6443 wrongly covers the released grpc 1.84 line, so govulncheck fails on any 1.84.x even though the fix is in it (golang/vulndb#6580). Remove once that report is corrected.

google.golang.org/api v0.299.0 requires grpc v1.84.0, so a security-tools group PR that takes it would drag grpc back onto the 1.84 line through `go mod tidy` and fail govulncheck. Goes away together with the grpc rule above.

Fleet's migrations and generated columns compute checksums with MySQL's MD5(), which MySQL removed in the 26.x line. Upstream Fleet tests only 8.0.44/8.4.8/9.5.0 and documents 9.6.0 as incompatible, so CI stays on the 8.4 LTS.
Left ungrouped so a Go stdlib security patch merges as its own PR, independent of regular dependency bumps.
